text:
nina_acme: Hey @jess_support — after our IDP rotated certs and the SSO refresh this morning I can no longer switch to the `acme-prod` project in the Console. Clicking the org/project shows a 403 permission denied. Deploys blocked, can we get an urgent escalation?

jess_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact error text you see and your login email? Is the 403 happening only in the UI or also API calls?

nina_acme: UI + API. Exact curl I ran (sanitized):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/orgs/acme/projects/acme-prod -i
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "permission_denied",
  "detail": "missing role: project.view"
}
```
My user email is nina@acme.com.

jess_support: Thanks — that response suggests your session token doesn't have the project role claims. Do you use SCIM group provisioning from Okta? If so, sometimes group-claim truncation or a change to the SAML attribute mapping can drop roles during an IDP refresh.

kevin_sre: Jumping in — I see a bunch of similar reports after the cert rotation window. Two quick checks: 1) confirm SCIM sync events for org `acme` returned non-empty groups for your user; 2) check the IDP assertion in the SSO logs for group claims (please redact PII). I'm going to trigger a resync for the org now.

jess_support: Workaround we can apply immediately if resync doesn't fix it: org admin (or we as support) can add you to the project via the admin API. Example admin call: 
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/orgs/acme/projects/acme-prod/members
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "email": "nina@acme.com",
  "role": "viewer"
}
```
That will restore console access without waiting on SCIM.

nina_acme: We asked IdP team to resync and I signed out/in. Still 403. Attaching last two lines from the Console auth log (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-17T08:12:03Z] auth: validate_saml_assertion user=xxx external_id=xxx groups=[]
[2026-03-17T08:12:03Z] auth: assign_roles none -> [] (no groups present)
```
So the assertion shows groups=[].

kevin_sre: Ok that explains it — SCIM/Assertion payload returned an empty groups array. I checked upstream SCIM events: Okta returned 200 for the user PATCH but the `groups` attribute was truncated and evaluated to empty on our side. Looks like the Okta group-claim hit the 256-char limit after the recent group renames. Root cause: IDP-side group filter/attribute length. Fix path: change Okta to send group IDs (shorter), or adjust the mapping to use a group filter rather than a long concatenated attribute.

emma_ops: For immediate mitigation, I've provisioned the user as a viewer on `acme-prod` via the admin API and created a support ticket to coordinate with the IdP team for a permanent fix.

jess_support: Done — I applied the admin API add (see internal action id: act-2026-849). Nina, can you try switching projects now?

nina_acme: Confirmed — can access `acme-prod` again and see project resources. Deploys unblocked. Thanks! :white_check_mark:

jess_support: Filing follow-up: ticket SUP-2026-451 created with recommended remediation steps for the IdP (map by group-id, remove long group list attribute, or enable SCIM full sync). We'll keep the temporary admin membership until your IdP confirms a safe mapping change.

kevin_sre: Added monitoring alert so we detect truncated group claims in future SCIM responses and auto-notify affected org owners.

deploy-bot: Incident note: incident-2026-03-17-ssosync created, severity=low, affected_orgs=["acme"], mitigated_by=admin-provisioning.

jess_support: Closing thread for now — reach out if the IdP change doesn't resolve it and we'll roll back the temporary member once SCIM is healthy. :)
